passage:
During English class, a student asked to open the window. The room was warm, but outside traffic was noisy.
Some students wanted fresh air. Others said the noise made listening difficult.
The teacher used the moment for discussion. The class tried three choices: window closed, window fully open, and window half open. They also changed seats to see if distance from the window mattered.
Finally, they chose to open the window halfway during writing time but close it during listening practice.
The problem was small, but the process was useful. Students learned that not every disagreement needs a winner. Sometimes the best answer depends on time, purpose, and compromise.
